shared_elements: low-relief carving on a large upright stone slab
figures shown in strict profile facing right/left
bent arm with hand and articulated fingers
areas of fine parallel incised lines / hatched texture (feathering in A, comb-like band in B)
elongated serpentine/tapering form (curving element near the legs in A, snake-like forms in B)
horizontal dividing lines splitting the surface into bands
justification: Both are shallow relief carvings on tall stone slabs using strict profile presentation, bent arms with splayed fingers, and passages of fine parallel hatching, and both are divided by horizontal lines into bands. However, A is dominated by a single large, anatomically detailed winged human figure filling the whole field, whereas B is a stepped, T-shaped block crowded with small, schematic, blocky animal forms in stacked registers — the compositional logic and level of naturalism are quite different.
